=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 101-104
```sh
pr_meta="$(gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "repos/${REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}" || echo 'null')"
pr_state="$(printf '%s\n' "${pr_meta}" | jq -r 'if ((.merged_at != null) or (.merged == true)) then "merged" else (.state // "") end' | grep -xE 'open|closed|merged' || echo "")"
if [ "${pr_state}" = "closed" ] || [ "${pr_state}" = "merged" ]; then
```
Problem: When `_safe_gh_jq` fails (network, rate-limit, malformed PR), the fallback `echo 'null'` gives jq a JSON null value. The `else` branch evaluates `.state // ""` on null → `""`, which fails the regex, and the final `|| echo ""` gives `pr_state=""`. Neither the "closed" nor "merged" branch is taken, so the PR-closed cleanup branch is silently skipped and the workflow continues into expensive reviewer/editor phases on a closed or merged PR.
Why it fails at runtime: A transient API failure during the PR metadata fetch causes the script to treat the PR as open (by omission) instead of closed/merged. The expensive metadata collection (four paginated API calls, large diff snapshots) and downstream reviewer prompt assembly proceed unnecessarily on a PR that has already merged or closed. The original version at least defaulted toward the cleanup path on any non-empty non-open string; the new version is strictly more fragile on API failures.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Correct fix: change the final fallback to `|| echo "open"` so that an API failure defaults to the open path (preserving the original intent of continuing on unknown state), while successful fetches still correctly detect closed/merged. Alternatively, add an explicit guard: `if [ -z "${pr_state}" ]; then echo "::warning::PR state unknown, assuming open"; pr_state="open"; fi`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
